page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor rated up to 4.2 GHz. The instance supplies 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It features 128.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU, alongside a 260 MB L3 cache. For local storage, the instance includes an integrated 1890 GB NVMe SSD, while GPU acceleration is not present.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate solid throughput across general compute and vector-accelerated tasks. The processor incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8, yielding strong performance in Geekbench image processing (14,706.0), text processing (2,617.0), and PassMark physics testing (7,174.99). Smaller LLM prompt processing achieves 2,518.71 tokens per second with text generation reaching top-tier levels of 355.44 tokens per second on a 135M model. General compute metrics, such as Geekbench multi-core (15,710.0), stress-ng multi-core (28,569.0), and PassMark CPU (47,243.56), land reliably in the middle 50% distribution.

The primary tradeoff lies in raw memory subsystem performance despite high compute capabilities. The PassMark memory score registered in the lower quartile (1,699.64), with uncached large-block write memory bandwidth measured at 55.49 GB/sec and read bandwidth at 138.52 GB/sec. However, static web serving throughput remains strong at 56.21 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations handle 46.62 million operations per second, supported by fast local NVMe storage and balanced core distribution.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the D32ds_v6 delivers solid density by bundling substantial NVMe scratch space and dedicated CPU cores without the premium associated with GPU-equipped instances. This makes the D32ds_v6 well fitted for general-purpose application workloads, relational and document database nodes needing local fast cache, medium-scale CI/CD build environments, web server fleets, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores with hyperthreading), 128.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core), and a bundled 1890 GB local NVMe SSD without discrete GPUs. Hardware support includes AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, driving strong results in static web serving (56.21 GB/sec) and lightweight LLM text generation (355.44 tokens/sec on 135M models). While multi-core compute and database operations perform consistently in mid-tier benchmarks, synthetic memory scores place in the lower quartile. The D32ds_v6 represents a balanced resource profile suitable for enterprise web serving, relational databases, Clang-based software compilation, and CPU-based inference workloads.
